# Public repo contribution inflow

Plan: `open-source-release-2026-09-29` (P-011). Decisions it rests on: D-003 (ELv2), D-004 (two repos, CLA not DCO, append-only public history).

## The model in one paragraph

`Papercusp/papercup` (private) is the **only** source of truth. `Papercusp/papercusp` (public, ELv2) is an **append-only export**: every public commit is produced by `node scripts/source-preview.mjs push --target public --confirm`, which re-exports a public-safe cut, runs the gate (secrets, identity, licence notices), and appends one commit on top of public `main` without `--force`. Nothing is ever merged directly on the public repo — a direct merge would be overwritten by the next export's tree and would bypass the gate.

## Flow for an outside pull request

1. **Triage on the public repo.** A maintainer reads the PR. Anything larger than a small fix should have had an issue first (CONTRIBUTING.md asks for this); if not, ask for one before reviewing in depth.
2. **CLA check.** CLA Assistant must show the author signed (individual or corporate CLA). No CLA → no port. Documentation typo fixes are exempt (CONTRIBUTING.md). The CLA is required because under ELv2 an inbound=outbound contribution would bind us by ELv2's own hosted-service limit (D-004 §2).
3. **Review the change as code, not as a patch file.** Same bar as internal work: tests in the project's framework, typecheck, no dependency whose licence conflicts with ELv2 (`scripts/check-licenses.mjs` enforces this on the export).
4. **Port it into the private tree.** Apply the PR diff to the canonical `staging` tree (`git apply` of `https://github.com/Papercusp/papercusp/pull/<N>.diff`, paths are identical because the export preserves layout). Register it as a work-item titled `Port public PR #<N>: <title>` and record the PR URL and the contributor's `Name <email>` (from the PR commits) on it. git-sync commits it like any other change; the private commit will NOT carry the contributor's identity (git-sync sweeps under one automation identity), which is why step 6 exists.
5. **Let it reach green `main`.** The public export defaults to `--ref main`, so the port ships only once the green checkpoint has promoted it.
6. **Ship it back out with credit.** Run
   `node scripts/source-preview.mjs push --target public --confirm --co-author "Name <email>"` (repeat `--co-author` for several contributors). This appends a public commit carrying a `Co-authored-by:` trailer per contributor, which GitHub renders as co-authorship. A malformed value is refused before any export work (`coAuthorTrailers` in `scripts/source-preview.mjs`, pinned by `packages/operator-core/lib/source-preview-sync.test.ts`).
7. **Close the PR** with a comment linking the public commit (`pushedCommit` in the push output) and thank the contributor. Close the port work-item citing the same commit.

If a contribution cannot be accepted (scope, licence, quality), close the PR with the reason; never leave it silently open.

## Changes that must not flow out

The export's selection (shared with the installer) already drops the closed set from D-004 §3 and anything the gate flags. A PR that edits a path absent from the public cut is either against a stale fork or touching something we do not publish — reject with an explanation rather than porting.

## Issue tracker policy

- **Public issues live on `Papercusp/papercusp`.** Maintainers mirror anything actionable into the private work-item ledger (`work_items:create`, with the issue URL in the body) and link back; the public issue is closed when the fix ships in an export, citing the public commit.
- **Private-only work stays private.** Internal work-items are not mirrored out; public issues are the only public tracker.
- **Security reports never go in public issues.** SECURITY.md points reporters to the private channel; handle those as private work-items and ship the fix before disclosure.
- Labels on the public repo are the minimum set: `bug`, `enhancement`, `question`, `good first issue`, `needs-cla`.

## Why not merge on GitHub

Merging on the public repo would (a) create public history the next append-only export does not descend from, so `pushSnapshot` would refuse with `public main moved during the push`, and (b) publish code that never passed the private test suite or the export gate. Porting keeps one source of truth and one gate.
